name: Chilled Water Plant & Distribution (Chillers / Cooling Towers / CHW Pumps / Loop) Installation, Flushing, Treatment & Balancing

activities: chiller and pump housekeeping plinths / inertia bases poured and cured
cooling tower structural deck / basin and dunnage steel ready
plant-room floor drainage, bund and trench formed
wall/slab sleeves and riser openings for CHW mains set
crane/rigging access and knock-out panel for chiller delivery confirmed
sequence.note: Civil scope is the enabler: inertia bases, tower dunnage, drainage bunds, sleeves and a lift path — all before any equipment lands.

activities: chillers rigged in and set on plinth / isolators
cooling towers assembled and set on deck
CHW / condenser pumps set on inertia bases
buffer tank set
sequence.note: Chillers are the heaviest, earliest heavy lift and fix the plant-room layout; pumps and towers follow. Delivery route must be preserved until units are in.

activities: pump/motor coupling alignment (laser)
baseplate grouting
chiller and tower levelling and anchoring
vibration isolator setting and check
sequence.note: Rotating equipment (pumps) needs coupling alignment and grouting before piping is connected, so piping strain does not distort alignment.

activities: primary/secondary CHW headers and mains erected
condenser-water piping to towers erected
riser and branch distribution to AHU/FCU coils installed
valves, strainers, balancing valves, pot feeder / dosing pot fitted
flexible connectors at pumps/chillers fitted last to avoid strain
sequence.note: Pipe is erected from plant outward; flexible connectors and final make-up to rotating equipment are fitted after alignment to avoid transmitting pipe strain.

activities: hydrostatic pressure test of CHW and condenser piping by section, witnessed
hold and inspect for weeps at joints/welds/flanges
sequence.note: Pressure test each section BEFORE insulation and before concealment above ceilings.

activities: chemical / mechanical flush of the loop to remove debris, mill scale, flux
temporary flushing bypasses / spool pieces across coils and chillers
strainer clean-out and re-check
flush to acceptable cleanliness before treatment
sequence.note: Flushing REQUIRES pressure test passed and full loop connected; coils and chillers are usually bypassed with spools to protect them during flushing.

activities: dose corrosion inhibitor / biocide / glycol to spec
condenser side: side-stream filtration and biocide dosing for towers
verify water chemistry (conductivity, pH, inhibitor level)
sequence.note: Treatment follows flushing — dosing dirty water wastes chemicals and fouls the loop; system is chemically stabilised before continuous running.

activities: CHW pipe thermal insulation with vapour barrier applied
valve/flange boxes and fittings insulated
condenser piping insulated where specified
sequence.note: Insulation follows a passed pressure test; vapour barrier integrity is critical on cold CHW pipe to prevent condensation.

activities: chiller, pump-motor and tower-fan power feeds terminated
VFDs / soft-starters connected and meggered
control wiring to valves, sensors, flow switches, DP transmitters landed
BMS I/O to plant terminated
sequence.note: Requires containment + cabling complete and power available; plant cannot run without energised feeders and live controls.

activities: pump solo run, rotation and vibration check
chiller manufacturer pre-start / oil, refrigerant charge, interlock checks
tower fan rotation and basin fill
flow-switch, DP and safety interlock verification
BMS point-to-point verification of the plant
sequence.note: Manufacturer's commissioning engineer attends chiller start; safety interlocks (flow, freeze, high-pressure) proven before first cooling.

activities: proportional balancing of the hydronic loop: set balancing valves to achieve design flow at each coil/branch
set primary/secondary pump speeds / VFD references
record flows, pump head, DP across the system
sequence.note: Water balancing REQUIRES flushing/treatment complete, pumps running and the full loop (all coils connected) — a partial loop cannot be balanced; coordinated with air-side TAB.

activities: chiller performance / capacity test at design conditions
sequencing and staging test (lead/lag, load-based staging)
integrated test with BMS: setpoint, reset schedules, plant enable/disable
cooling tower approach and condenser-water performance test
full-load and part-load performance verification
sequence.note: Final commissioning integrates chillers, towers, pumps and BMS under load; depends on a live BMS, energised plant and a balanced, treated loop, plus a heat load (real or artificial) to prove capacity.

typical_relationships.before: Chiller/pump inertia bases and plinths poured and cured
typical_relationships.reason: Heavy rotating equipment must land on a cured foundation/inertia base sized for its weight and dynamic loads.

typical_relationships.before: Pump-motor coupling aligned and baseplate grouted
typical_relationships.reason: Piping is made up after alignment so pipe weight and thermal strain do not pull the pump out of alignment.
A section must be physically complete and closed before it can be filled and pressure-tested.
Flushing a loop that has not been proven leak-tight risks spraying and re-work; test integrity first.
Dosing inhibitor into a dirty loop wastes chemicals and lets debris continue to foul; clean before dosing.

typical_relationships.after: Pipe thermal insulation and vapour barrier
typical_relationships.reason: Insulation conceals joints; testing after insulating means stripping insulation to reach a leak.

typical_relationships.before: Flushing bypass spools across chiller/coils fitted
typical_relationships.reason: Chillers and coils are isolated with spool pieces so flushing debris does not lodge in their tubes.

typical_relationships.before: Pump power and controls terminated and meggered
typical_relationships.reason: A motor cannot be energised for rotation/vibration check until its feeder and protection are connected and insulation-tested.

typical_relationships.before: Flushing and water treatment complete; pumps running; full loop connected
typical_relationships.reason: Design flows can only be set on a clean, treated, fully-connected loop with pumps running; a partial or dirty loop gives invalid balance.
Running a chiller without proven flow and safety interlocks risks freeze/mechanical damage; interlocks come first.

typical_relationships.after: Chiller performance and plant sequencing commissioning
typical_relationships.reason: Capacity and staging tests assume design flow through evaporators/coils, so balancing must finish first.

typical_relationships.before: BMS point-to-point verified on the plant
typical_relationships.reason: Lead/lag staging and reset schedules are executed by the BMS, which must have verified control of every plant point first.

typical_relationships.before: Cooling tower basin filled and treated
typical_relationships.after: Condenser-water pump run and chiller start (water-cooled)
typical_relationships.reason: A water-cooled chiller needs condenser water circulating from a filled, treated tower before it can reject heat.

interfaces.requirement: Chiller/pump inertia bases and plinths, cooling-tower dunnage/deck, plant-room drainage bunds, riser openings and rigging access must be complete before equipment delivery and setting.
CHW/condenser pumps follow rotating-equipment practice: coupling alignment and grouting before piped connection, flexible connectors to decouple pipe strain.
Chillers, pump motors and tower fans require permanent (or commissioning) power feeders energised and VFDs/starters connected before any run.
Power and control cabling to the plant requires containment installed and cables pulled and terminated first.
Plant control points (valves, DP, flow, temperature, VFD refs) must be BMS-verified point-to-point so the BMS can stage plant and drive balancing and sequencing tests.
Flow switches, DP transmitters, temperature sensors and safety interlocks must be installed and calibrated before chiller start and balancing.
Chilled water supplies AHU/FCU cooling coils; air-side temperature commissioning and TAB depend on CHW being flushed, treated, balanced and available.
Make-up water supply and drainage capacity are required to fill, flush and dispose of flushing water for the loop and cooling towers.
CHW pipe insulation with vapour barrier is applied only after the hydrostatic test passes.
Distribution mains and risers share pipe-rack and riser space; CHW routing must be coordinated with other piping and supports.
A heat load (real building load or artificial load bank / temporary heater) plus stable permanent power is needed to prove chiller capacity at design conditions.

testing_requirements: Hydrostatic pressure test of CHW and condenser-water piping by section, witnessed, before insulation/concealment
System flushing and cleanliness verification (before treatment)
Water chemistry / treatment verification (inhibitor level, pH, conductivity, glycol %)
Pump-motor insulation resistance (megger) test before energisation
Pump coupling alignment record and vibration check on solo run
Chiller manufacturer pre-start checks (refrigerant charge, oil, interlocks) and start-up report
Safety interlock verification: flow switch, freeze stat, high-pressure cut-out
BMS point-to-point (I/O) verification for all plant control points
Hydronic water balancing report: measured vs design flow at each coil/branch, pump head, DP
Chiller capacity / performance test at design and part-load conditions
Plant sequencing / staging (lead-lag) functional test with BMS
Cooling tower approach and condenser-water performance test (water-cooled)
commissioning_dependencies: Permanent (or commissioning) power energised to chillers, pumps and tower fans
Loop pressure-tested, flushed, cleaned and chemically treated
Full loop connected (all coils/AHUs) so flow can be balanced
BMS live with verified plant control points for staging and reset
Instrumentation and safety interlocks installed and calibrated
Cooling tower filled and treated (water-cooled plant) with condenser water circulating
Make-up water and drainage available for fill/flush
A heat load (real or artificial) available to prove chiller capacity
Water balancing complete before chiller performance and sequencing tests
Coordinated with air-side TAB so water and air balancing align

work_packages.note: interfaces with civil for bases and rigging
interfaces with electrical_power, containment_cabling, bms, instrumentation

typical_exceptions: Air-cooled chillers omit cooling towers and condenser-water piping entirely, dropping the tower and CW stages.
Packaged/skid-mounted plant arrives with pumps, pipework and controls pre-assembled, collapsing several field stages into set-and-connect.
Small systems may use a single primary-only pumping arrangement with no secondary loop or buffer tank.
Glycol systems add a freeze-protection dosing step and change the water-treatment acceptance.
District-cooling-fed buildings have no on-site chillers — the interface becomes an energy-transfer station (heat exchanger) and the chiller start stages do not apply.
evidence: Hydronic water balancing, chiller capacity testing or plant sequencing is scheduled before the loop is flushed, treated and fully connected with the BMS live — so measured flows and capacities cannot be valid; or pipe insulation/concealment precedes the witnessed hydrostatic test, or the pump is piped up before coupling alignment and grouting.
